exercise1.prompt: Summing and Axes: One total per student

hiddenCases.name: a single row totals on its own
the totals are per row, not per column

exercise1.hint: One total per student means one per row, so the sum has to collapse across the columns. That is axis=1.

exercise2.prompt: Summing and Axes: The hardest test

hiddenCases.name: the first column can be the hardest
a single test is the answer by default

exercise2.hint: table.mean(axis=0) gives one mean per test. argmin on that gives the position of the smallest. Wrap it in int() so the answer is a plain number.

questions.prompt: For a table of students down and tests across, which gives one total per student?
questions.explain: One per student means one per row, so the columns are what collapses. axis=1 is across.
It names what is removed, which is why axis=0 — the row dimension — leaves one value per column.

questions.prompt: table.sum() with no axis on a 2-D array gives what?
questions.explain: With no axis named there is nothing left to keep, so everything collapses.

questions.prompt: You expected two numbers and got three. What is the quickest diagnosis?
choices: The axis is the wrong way round
questions.explain: The length of the result tells you which dimension survived. This is why checking the shape beats reading the numbers.
